data_scope.spatial_coverage: United States only; nationally representative US adult samples
data_scope.primary_model: GPT-4 (training-data cutoff predating publication of many archive studies)
data_scope.replication_models: prominent open-weight models (names not stated in accessible text)
data_scope.data_code_availability: Code Ocean capsule 9843791 v1; Source Data XLSX for Figs. 1-3 and Extended Data Figs. 2-3; public demo at treatmenteffect.app

core_conclusion: Prompted to simulate demographically diverse American respondents, GPT-4 predicted treatment effects across 70 preregistered nationally representative US survey experiments (469 effects, 119,330 participants) at accuracy comparable to pooled human forecasts, with correlations holding for studies published after the model's training cutoff and for prominent open-weight models. Predictions nevertheless systematically overestimate effect sizes, so the usable signal is rank ordering rather than magnitude. On a harder secondary archive of 15 megastudies (606 effects) accuracy fell but remained comparable to pooled expert forecasters, supporting augmentation of experimental methods rather than replacement of human participants.
why_it_matters: Shifts LLM social simulation from reproducing survey marginals to recovering causal estimates; the training-cutoff split rules out memorization; the honest finding of high correlation with inflated magnitudes defines correct use (screening, not substitution); changes the economics of pilot testing, intervention selection and replication triage; and pairs the technical result with a 460-scientist survey plus bias and misuse analyses.
why_nature: A methodological intervention into how an entire discipline runs experiments, not a single finding within it; archive-scale preregistered evidence spanning 1,075 effects; built-in falsification via the training-cutoff and open-weight tests; benefits reported alongside bias, misuse and community-norm analyses; and immediate translation through open data, code and a public forecasting demo.
added_value_to_my_research: Geo-conditioned personas -> synthetic response propensities keyed to census tracts as behavioural demand weights in 2SFCA/R2SFCA
Hierarchical recalibration of inflated effect sizes -> decision-grade intervals for my spatial ML accessibility predictions
LLM behavioural prior x agent-based/SIR spatial diffusion -> message-to-uptake pipeline for telehealth and vaccination campaigns
Subgroup rank-fidelity threshold -> equity guardrail before any LLM prior enters health-access or facility-siting decisions
Prompt-ensemble scaling law + SHAP-style attribution -> compute budgeting and explainability for geospatial foundation-model ensembles
